articles.title: China ha finalizado una revolución más inquietante que sus tierras raras: la aparición de cientos de agujeros en sus desiertos
articles.text:
En plena Guerra Fría, Estados Unidos y la Unión Soviética aprendieron que la mejor forma de evitar una guerra nuclear era convencer al enemigo de que nunca podría destruir todas sus armas de un solo golpe. Medio siglo después, cientos de nuevos agujeros aparecidos en los desiertos de China sugieren que Pekín ha llegado exactamente a la misma conclusión.
La revolución estaba bajo tierra. Durante la última década, buena parte de la atención sobre el poder militar chino se ha concentrado en sus cazas furtivos, sus portaaviones o sus misiles hipersónicos. Sin embargo, el cambio más profundo y potencialmente más trascendente ha ocurrido lejos de los focos, en los desiertos del oeste del país.
Allí, imágenes por satélite han revelado la aparición de centenares de nuevos silos para misiles nucleares, una transformación que muchos analistas consideran la mayor expansión del arsenal estratégico chino de toda su historia y que marca un cambio radical en la forma en que Pekín concibe su disuasión nuclear.
Los desiertos chinos y los silos. El punto de inflexión llegó en 2021, cuando investigadores especializados en inteligencia de fuentes abiertas detectaron la construcción de enormes campos de silos cerca de Yumen, Hami y Ordos.
Solo esas tres zonas suman alrededor de 320 nuevas instalaciones, una cifra sin precedentes para un país que históricamente había mantenido un arsenal relativamente reducido. Estados Unidos cree que todos esos silos acabarán albergando misiles, mientras que otros expertos plantean que algunos podrían permanecer vacíos para dificultar que un adversario sepa cuáles contienen armas reales y cuáles son señuelos.
Cambio de filosofía. Durante décadas, la estrategia nuclear china se basó en disponer de un número limitado de misiles capaces de garantizar una represalia si era atacada. Ahora el objetivo parece diferente: aumentar el tamaño del arsenal, dispersarlo y hacerlo mucho más difícil de destruir en un primer golpe.
Lo hemos contado antes. La combinación de silos endurecidos, lanzadores móviles y nuevas tecnologías busca asegurar que, incluso tras un ataque masivo, China conserve capacidad suficiente para responder, reforzando así el efecto disuasorio de sus fuerzas estratégicas.
Una fuerza móvil y preparada. La evolución tecnológica refleja ese cambio doctrinal. Los antiguos DF-5, alimentados con combustible líquido y desplegados en silos, continúan en servicio tras varias modernizaciones, pero el protagonismo ha pasado a la familia DF-31 y, sobre todo, al DF-41.
Estos misiles utilizan combustible sólido, pueden desplazarse sobre grandes vehículos lanzadores y entrar en acción mucho más rápido, reduciendo enormemente su vulnerabilidad. Además, varias versiones incorporan cabezas nucleares múltiples independientes (MIRV), lo que permite que un solo misil ataque varios objetivos distintos.
La tríada nuclear china al completo. Los misiles terrestres son solo una parte del plan. Pekín también está reforzando su componente naval con los submarinos de la clase Type 094 y los futuros Type 096, equipados con los misiles JL-2 y el más avanzado JL-3, que permitirá atacar territorio continental estadounidense desde aguas mucho más próximas a China.
Paralelamente continúa el desarrollo del bombardero furtivo H-20, destinado a completar una tríada nuclear plenamente operativa, es decir, la capacidad de lanzar armas nucleares desde tierra, mar y aire.
Complicar cualquier defensa. La modernización no consiste únicamente en fabricar más misiles. China trabaja en vehículos hipersónicos de planeo capaces de maniobrar a gran velocidad tras su lanzamiento, dificultando enormemente su interceptación.
El nuevo DF-61 podría convertirse en el primer misil intercontinental chino diseñado para emplear este tipo de armas. A ello se suman sistemas de penetración, mejoras en precisión y plataformas móviles capaces de ocultarse y desplazarse continuamente, incrementando la incertidumbre para cualquier adversario.
Una nueva etapa. El Pentágono estima que China ya supera las 600 cabezas nucleares operativas y que podría rebasar las 1.000 antes de 2030. Más importante que la cifra es la velocidad de la transformación: en apenas unos años, Pekín ha pasado de mantener una fuerza nuclear relativamente modesta a construir una estructura comparable, en algunos aspectos, a la de las otras grandes potencias atómicas.
Los cientos de silos que han ido apareciendo silenciosamente en el desierto son la prueba física de ese cambio y el recordatorio de que la revolución militar más importante de China quizá no haya ocurrido en el aire ni en el mar, sino bajo tierra.

articles.title: Synology Expands All-Flash Enterprise Storage Lineup With the New FlashStation FS6420
articles.text:
Wednesday, July 29th 2026
	
		
	
	
	Synology Expands All-Flash Enterprise Storage Lineup With the New FlashStation FS6420
Synology today announced the FlashStation FS6420, the newest addition to its all-flash server lineup. Delivering exceptional throughput, it is designed for performance-intensive workloads, including virtual machine storage and protection, file synchronization, and business application hosting.
"The FS6420 meets the increasing need for fast, responsive storage in data-intensive environments," said Susan Yen, Product Manager at Synology. "With unified NAS and SAN capabilities, it provides a flexible storage platform for organizations running a wide range of workloads without the complexity of managing separate infrastructures."All-flash enterprise performance and proven reliability
Built for high-concurrency workloads, the FS6420 delivers over 929,000/257,000 4K random read/write IOPS. It comes equipped with dual 10GbE ports and supports optional 25GbE or Fiber Channel network adapters, enabling seamless integration into modern high-speed infrastructures.
Beyond performance, the FS6420 includes a comprehensive set of availability features designed to ensure service continuity and safeguard critical data. Dedicated out-of-band (OOB) management, network failover and load balancing, hot-swappable redundant power supplies, and support for high-availability clustering help maintain uninterrupted operations during routine maintenance and unexpected outages.
Versatile features for business workloads
Powered by DiskStation Manager (DSM), FS6420 offers a comprehensive suite of features designed to meet the evolving data management needs of any business.
Synology Virtual Machine Manager and Container Manager provide VM storage, backup, and hosting, fully certified for VMware, Hyper-V, Citrix, and OpenStack, and enable lightweight VMs or containers for testing, sandboxing, and emergency recovery.
Synology Tiering optimizes storage economics by automatically moving infrequently accessed data between performance and capacity tiers, helping organizations optimize storage costs.
Synology Drive transforms the system into a private cloud, enabling cross-platform access and site-to-site syncing for distributed teams.
Availability
The FS6420 will be available starting 29 July 2026, through Synology's network of partners and resellers worldwide.

articles.title: Cloud observability startup Groundcover raises $100M in funding - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cloud observability startup Groundcover raises $100M in funding
Groundcover Inc., a startup with a platform for monitoring cloud environments, today announced that it has raised $100 million in funding.
One Peak led the Series C round. It was joined by Morgan Stanley, Zeev Ventures, Angular Ventures, Heavybit and Jibe. CTech reported that the deal values Groundcover at $500 million.
Many observability tools charge users based on the amount of telemetry they collect. That pricing model often leads companies to limit the number of workloads they monitor in the interest of lowering costs. For example, a software startup might decide not to monitor a development environment that doesn’t contain any sensitive data.
Troubleshooting an outage without telemetry about the affected workload can be challenging. Furthermore, visibility gaps make it more difficult to spot cyberattacks. According to Groundcover, its observability platform addresses those challenges with a pricing model that isn’t tied to the amount of data users ingest. That makes it possible to collect telemetry from low-priority workloads which would otherwise be too expensive to monitor.
Under the hood, Groundcover collects telemetry using a technology called eBPF. It’s a component of Linux, the operating system that powers most public cloud environments.
The core components of Linux are stored in a module known as the operating system kernel. The kernel plays a role in practically every action that the applications running on top perform. As a result, it possesses detailed data about those applications. Groundcover uses eBPF to collect the observability data that the Linux kernel generates.
Turning the Linux kernel into an observability mechanism requires developers to extend it with custom code. Usually, the task is prohibitively complicated because operating system modifications often lead to reliability and cybersecurity issues. That’s where eBPF comes into the picture. It runs kernel extensions in an isolated sandbox that mitigates common reliability issues.
Groundcover says that its eBPF-powered telemetry collection sensor can be installed in a few minutes. Furthermore, developers don’t have to modify the applications they wish to monitor. Customers can optionally enrich their eBPF data using OpenTelemetry, a popular observability tool that does require code modifications.
“We offer full-fidelity telemetry, unsampled, across infrastructure, applications, and AI workloads, captured by an eBPF sensor with no code changes and no instrumentation,” Groundcover Chief Executive Officer Shahar Azulay (pictured, right, with Chief Technology Officer Yechezkel Rabinovich) wrote in a blog post.
Groundcover’s platform can ingest telemetry data at a rate of several gigabytes per second. It collects logs, metrics and traces. The software organizes the data in a format that makes it simpler to determine which record describes what application.
Some observability platforms keep telemetry in a managed storage environment. By contrast, Groundcover enables customers to keep telemetry in their own public cloud deployments. The company says that its approach improves cybersecurity and creates opportunities to lower costs. In particular, customers can keep new logs in high-performance flash drives and move historical data to less expensive cold storage.
Groundcover says that its platform is used by more than 250 organizations. Several of those customers signed seven-figure deals with the software maker in the past year.
Groundcover will use much of its newly raised funding to accelerate its go-to-market efforts in North America. Additionally, the company plans to grow its international presence and enhance its partner program. Groundwork’s efforts in the latter area will place particular emphasis on joint sales initiatives with cloud providers.

articles.text:
Galaxy Watch Ultra com tela AMOLED despenca 67% em oferta de Dia dos Pais
Ideal para pais esportistas, o Galaxy Watch Ultra com GPS integrado e até 80 horas de bateria tem amplo desconto com cupom exclusivo do app Magalu
Ideal para pais esportistas, o Galaxy Watch Ultra com GPS integrado e até 80 horas de bateria tem amplo desconto com cupom exclusivo do app Magalu
Após o anúncio do sucessor, o Galaxy Watch Ultra entrou em oferta por R$ 1.664,10 no Pix com o cupom BLACKAPP150, exclusivo do aplicativo Magalu. Lançado por R$ 4.999, o smartwatch esportivo com display AMOLED e conexão 4G LTE sai por menos da metade do preço e pode ser um ótimo presente para o Dia dos Pais.
O Galaxy Watch Ultra adota uma tela Super AMOLED de 1,5 polegadas com proteção em vidro de Cristal de Safira e brilho máximo de 3.000 nits, facilitando a visualização em qualquer ambiente. Igual ao sucessor Watch Ultra 2, o relógio tem caixa de titânio de 47 mm com botões e coroa giratória para navegar pelos menus do sistema Wear OS do Google.
O dispositivo projetado para esportistas e aventureiros consegue monitorar atividades físicas diversas, como caminhada, corrida, ciclismo e natação. Já o GPS integrado é essencial para mapear trajetos em treinos ao ar livre e receber indicação de direção durante trilhas.
Aqui vale citar que o Galaxy Watch Ultra oferece conexão 4G LTE via eSim, permitindo que o usuário esteja sempre conectado em qualquer lugar com sinal de rede móvel. Algo que reduz a dependência de um smartphone Galaxy ou rede Wi-Fi para acessar a internet.
O smartwatch esportivo da Samsung também conta com o sensor de saúde BioActive, que registra dados de frequência cardíaca, pressão arterial, padrões de sono e outros detalhes. Essas informações podem ser sincronizadas com o Samsung Health, aplicativo que ajuda a criar um histórico de saúde e atividades do usuário.
Em relação à autonomia, o relógio oferece entre 60 horas (com o recurso Always On Display) e 80 horas de uso. O modelo tem recurso de recarga rápida sem fio com base de indução no padrão WPC.
Mesmo com 2 GB de RAM e 64 GB de armazenamento, o Galaxy Watch Ultra (R$ 1.664,10 no Pix com o cupom BLACKAPP150 no app) traz suporte ao Galaxy AI e ao Google Gemini. Na parte de conexões, o modelo tem Bluetooth 5.3 e NFC para ações por aproximação.

articles.title: Cuánta memoria RAM debería tener tu celular según el tipo de usuario que eres
articles.text:
Dentro de la gran cantidad de características que hoy tiene un celular, la memoria RAM es clave para entender el rendimiento del teléfono. Sin embargo, dentro del rango de opciones que hay no siempre es necesario ir por el más potente.
Aunque actualmente hay grandes cifras de 24 GB o 32 GB de RAM, también hay alternativas de 4 y 6 GB que se adaptan bien para aquellos usuarios menos exigentes y demandantes.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué es la memoria RAM
La memoria RAM (Random Access Memory) permite que el teléfono mantenga abiertas varias aplicaciones al mismo tiempo y gestione procesos en segundo plano sin cierres inesperados.
No determina la velocidad absoluta del procesador, pero sí la capacidad del sistema para responder de forma ágil cuando saltamos entre apps, juegos o tareas de inteligencia artificial. Por eso, conocer el perfil de usuario resulta clave para evitar pagar de más por prestaciones que la mayoría nunca llegará a utilizar.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué tipo de memoria RAM se adapta mejor a cada usuario
El tipo de usuario es el factor que más influye en la cantidad de RAM que debe tener un smartphone. Las recomendaciones actuales dividen a los usuarios en cinco grandes categorías, cada una con demandas y límites concretos:
- Usuario muy básico (4 GB):
Se trata de quienes utilizan el teléfono para llamadas, WhatsApp y navegación simple. Aunque en 2026 todavía existen modelos de entrada con 4 GB, esta cifra resulta insuficiente incluso para las tareas más simples. Las aplicaciones se recargan constantemente y la multitarea es prácticamente inexistente. No es una opción recomendable para el entorno actual.
PUBLICIDAD
- Usuario básico (6 GB):
Quienes usan mensajería, redes sociales y navegan ocasionalmente pueden optar por 6 GB. Sin embargo, deberán cerrar apps en segundo plano con frecuencia y notarán restricciones al alternar entre tareas.
- Usuario promedio (8 GB):
Con 8 GB de RAM, el usuario disfruta de una multitarea fluida, streaming sin interrupciones, juegos casuales y funciones de inteligencia artificial básicas. Resulta suficiente para mantener abiertas varias aplicaciones populares —Instagram, YouTube, WhatsApp, navegador— sin que el sistema las cierre para liberar recursos.
PUBLICIDAD
- Usuario avanzado o gamer (12 GB):
Quienes usan el teléfono para juegos exigentes como Genshin Impact o Call of Duty Mobile, edición ligera de fotos y vídeos, o alternan entre más de una docena de apps abiertas, se benefician de los 12 GB. Esta configuración permite una multitarea intensiva y acelera tareas relacionadas con la creación de contenido o el uso profesional del móvil.
- Power user y creadores de contenido (16 GB o más):
Solo aquellos que editan vídeo en 4K/8K, utilizan modelos de inteligencia artificial localmente, requieren experiencias tipo escritorio (como Samsung DeX) o prevén mantener el dispositivo más de cuatro años, necesitan 16 GB o más. Para la mayoría, esa capacidad resulta innecesaria y no se percibe en el día a día.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué tan necesario es tener mucha memoria RAM
Algunos fabricantes ya ofrecen teléfonos con 24 GB o 32 GB de RAM. Estas cifras responden principalmente a estrategias de marketing y no a una necesidad técnica real. Ninguna aplicación móvil —ni siquiera los juegos más exigentes— demanda tanta memoria.
El exceso de RAM no se traduce en mayor velocidad ni en mejor experiencia de usuario; muchas veces, el sobreprecio podría invertirse en componentes que sí mejoran el rendimiento, como el procesador, la pantalla o la batería.
PUBLICIDAD
Pero antes de decidir qué cantidad de RAM comprar, es fundamental mirar otros aspectos, como el procesador. Este aspecto determina en gran parte cómo se gestiona la memoria; un chip de gama alta (como Snapdragon 8 Gen 4, Dimensity 9400 o A19 Pro) aprovecha mejor la RAM, incluso si la cantidad no es la más alta del mercado.
La optimización del software también juega un papel clave. Un iPhone con 8 GB puede mantener abiertas tantas aplicaciones como un Android con 12 GB, gracias a la gestión eficiente de procesos en iOS.

articles.title: ‘The trend towards automated, hands-free household cleaning is inevitable,’ says Dreame exec — so why aren't robot vacuums mainstream yet?
articles.text:
What's stopping robot vacuums from going mainstream? I grilled execs from five of the biggest brands to find out
What’s holding these handy home bots back?
Robot vacuums have been around for many years, and modern bots are cleverer and more helpful than ever. But while they are getting more popular, they seem to be struggling to properly break through to the mainstream. See a robot vacuum in someone's house, and you'd probably still remark on it. The aim for robovac brands must be to at some point overtake manual vacs as the general public's dust-sucker of choice — so why isn't that happening?
I rounded up representatives from some of the best robot vacuum brands to get their take. I wanted to learn more about the misconceptions that brands are still fighting against, how perceptions of these handy puck-shaped home helpers has changed, and what challenges still remain if robovacs are going to truly hit the mainstream.
Get with the times
"Robot vacuums are gradually being accepted and adopted by the public, rather than being treated as a novel and unrealistic concept," insists Michael Meng, president of the robotic vacuum division at Dreame.
"Admittedly, the market share of robot vacuums is still smaller than that of stick vacuums and upright vacuums, but the trend towards automated, hands-free household cleaning is inevitable," he adds. The problem — as all of my interviewees agree — is that people's perceptions are stuck in the past.
"The issue isn't technical — it's psychological," says Faraz Mehdi, a managing director at Eufy. "Many people who've used robot vacuums still associate the category with 'mopping with dirty water' and 'poor carpet cleaning' — real pain points from a few years ago. Today's products are fundamentally different."
"One lingering misconception is that robot vacuums are still novelty gadgets that wander randomly, get stuck constantly, and cannot clean as well as a conventional vacuum. That perception often comes from earlier generations of the category," says Ricky Ma, the general manager for Europe and America at Roborock.
He continues: "The biggest opportunity is helping consumers understand that a robot vacuum is not simply a smaller vacuum; it is an automated, intelligent cleaning system designed to maintain the home every day and free up their time in a way that no other appliance can compete with."
"Ultimately, the industry's continued growth will depend not only on technological innovation but also on helping consumers better understand how far the category has evolved," adds Dreame's Meng. "Bridging the gap between perception and reality remains one of the most important opportunities for the industry as a whole."
Welcome to the real world
So there are unfair assumptions about modern robot vacuum performance, but there are also genuine issues that still need to be solved. As a robovac reviewer, I'm regularly struck by how simultaneously smart and stupid these bots can be — for every bot raising itself majestically over a tall room threshold, there's another determinedly head-butting a French door.
I'm in wholehearted agreement with Reena Patel — a floorcare category manager at iRobot, the brand behind Roomba — when she suggests that autonomy and reliability should be the key focus areas.
"While robot vacuums have become significantly smarter, consumers still expect them to navigate increasingly complex environments, avoid everyday obstacles, handle pet hair effectively, and transition seamlessly between different floor types without intervention," she says.
"The goal is to deliver consistently excellent cleaning results while reducing the need for maintenance, ensuring the robot can truly operate as a set-and-forget solution that fits effortlessly into consumers' daily lives."
Minimal human intervention is one of the hot robot vacuum trends du jour, but it's easier said than done. Mehdi points out that, in the UK at least, plenty of people live in old apartments or multi-story homes, both of which are "historically a nightmare for robots". Throw in challenges like clutter, low-slung furniture, uneven flooring, and mixtures of different floor types, and it's easy to see why people might assume a robot vacuum wouldn't be able to cope.
There are solutions to some of these problems — albeit mostly confined to the premium end of the market. Today's most advanced flagship robots have features like little stilts for vaulting tall thresholds, sensors that identify and respond to different surfaces, and slimline designs that can sneak under furniture.
However, the challenge is to hone those features to a point where they work consistently and reliably. After all, if, your bot misjudges the height of a space and gets itself wedged, or fails to cross a step on the way back to its dock, and you're not around to bail it out, that can put a pretty abrupt end to the cleaning for the day.
"It’s one thing for a robot to perform well in a demo, but another to perform reliably, day after day, in homes that are busy, messy, and unpredictable," admits Mehdi. "The real issue isn't what the product can do, it's that consumers haven't seen it perform in their own space."
The bigger picture
The robot vacuum market has evolved considerably in the past few years, but so too has what customers are looking for. All my interviewees agreed lofty specs are no longer the route to a customer's heart (or wallet).
"Customers are looking beyond headline suction figures and realize that the performance of robot vacuums is the combination of a lot of features," says Dreame's Meng.
Eufy's Mehdi echoes his sentiments: "A few years ago, the category was often marketed around isolated features like suction power. But consumers are now evaluating robot vacuums much more holistically. People are looking for real cleaning outcomes, not just bigger numbers on a spec sheet."
Expectations are also rising — a number of the brands I spoke to told me that customers increasingly want bots that can mop as well as vacuuming, and are looking for models with self-maintenance features like dust-emptying, water tank refilling, and mop washing.
iRobot's Patel comments that customers are "more willing to purchase premium robot vacuums to deliver a genuinely hands-off experience".
Dreame's Meng argues that the move from cheap-and-basic to pricey-and-advanced bots reflects a change in perceptions. "Users are starting to realize that they can trust robot vacuums to take on more of their household cleaning."
Pricier bots might be becoming more popular, but customers aren't willing to splash their cash on just anything. Mehdi at Eufy describes a demand for "flagship-level experiences… at broader price points", noting that even at the upper end of the market, people are "rational about value".
"The market is shifting towards products that deliver meaningful innovation people can actually use and justify paying for," he explains.
As part of this trend, the early adopters who took a leap of faith with a simpler model a few years ago are now ready for something more advanced. "We have observed a significant shift from 'first-time experimenters' to 'sophisticated upgraders'," Roborock's Ma tells me.
These shoppers are seeking out replacements that solve the issues that frustrated them with their first bot. Thanks to design innovations, many problems that plagued early robot vacuums — hair tangling, poor edge coverage and stinky mop pads — are far less common in modern models.
Not your average robovac
Features and price decisions aside, my interviewees have noticed a broader change in purchasing habits — and it's tied to how people see robot vacuums. "More consumers are treating robot vacuums as long-term home automation investments rather than one-off gadgets," says Richard Mou, co-founder of SwitchBot. "They're spending more time comparing ecosystem compatibility, software updates, and after-sales support before making a purchase."
Mehdi describes a dovetailing of approaches. At the upper end of the market, he's noticed customers going really in-depth with the research and product comparison, while at the more affordable end of the market, the decision-making process is different.
"There, trust can matter more than technical comparisons," he says. "Ratings, reviews, brand reputation, and recommendations from friends or family are often more influential than specs alone."
"That tells us something important about where the category is today," he concludes. "As robot vacuums become more mainstream, people are evaluating them less like gadgets and more like long-term home appliances."
So robot vacuums are getting smarter, customers are starting to embrace the modern advancements now on offer, and brands are working to address the pain-points that still linger when it comes to using a robovac in a real, messy, haphazard home.
The fact that people are viewing their robot vacuums as investment purchases rather than short-lived impulse purchases suggests things are moving in the right direction. Perhaps we will yet see a future where, when we see a robot vacuum in the corner of a room, it'll no longer be worthy of comment.

articles.title: GMKtec launches the Evo-X1 Pro mini PC with Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 — and it already has an early bird deal
articles.text:
GMKtec launches the new Evo-X1 Pro mini PC with Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 and OCuLink — and it already has an early bird deal
The AI mini PC packs 64GB of RAM, Radeon 890M graphics, and a 55 TOPS NPU inside the chassis.
GMKtec has just launched the Evo-X1 Pro, a premium AI-focused mini PC built around AMD's new Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 chip, 64GB LPDDR5 RAM, with an OCuLink port that lets you bolt on a full desktop GPU when you need more graphics power. To mark the new release, readers in the US and the UK can save on the launch price with this Early Bird discount.
The 1TB Evo-X1 Pro is now $1580 (was $1600), while the 2TB model is $1750 (was $1770). Meanwhile, in the UK, the GMKtec Evo X1-Pro 1TB drops to £1230 (was £1250), with the 2TB config running to £1360 (was £1380).
I'm particularly excited because the previous model proved to be an incredible powerhouse that scored 4.5 stars in our review - and I reckon this upgrade is going to be an even bigger beast.
Today's top GMKtec mini PC deal
Built around AMD's Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 (12 cores, 24 threads, boosting to 5.2GHz) with Radeon 890M integrated graphics and a dedicated NPU rated up to 55 TOPS. This configuration comes with 64GB of LPDDR5X-6400 memory and a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD, with a second M.2 slot free for expansion. A 2TB config is also on sale.
In the UK: now £1230 (was £1250)
Offer ends August 15
The Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 is a Zen 5-based chip with 12 cores and 24 threads, 24MB of L3 cache, and boost speeds up to 5.2GHz — a step up from the mid-range mini PCs we usually see in this category.
It pairs that with AMD's XDNA 2 NPU, which GMKtec rates at up to 55 TOPS on its own, or up to 86 TOPS when combined with the rest of the system, aimed at running local AI models and LLM workloads directly on the machine rather than in the cloud.
Graphics come from AMD's Radeon 890M, based on RDNA 3.5 with 16 compute units — enough for mainstream AAA gaming at moderate settings without a discrete card.
The standout feature here is the OCuLink port, a PCIe 4.0 x4 connection that lets you attach an external desktop GPU when you want considerably more graphics performance for gaming or GPU-accelerated AI and creative work. GMKtec notes OCuLink doesn't support hot-swapping, so any external GPU needs to be connected or disconnected with the system powered off.
Memory tops out at 64GB of LPDDR5X-6400, and storage is handled by dual M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 x4 slots supporting up to 8TB combined, so there's real room to grow beyond the 1TB or 2TB the machine ships with.
GMKtec is pairing this hardware with what it calls an Arctic Cooling System — a dual-fan setup with a dedicated CPU cooler, a separate system fan, dual air intakes, and dust-resistant construction, designed to keep the machine both cool and quiet during sustained AI or gaming workloads.
Connectivity is generous for the category: up front you get USB4, two USB-A 3.2 Gen2 ports, the OCuLink port, and a 3.5mm audio jack, while the rear adds HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 2.1, and two more USB-A 3.2 Gen2 ports. Triple-display output is supported at up to 8K resolution. Networking covers dual 2.5GbE LAN and Wi-Fi 7, which should comfortably outpace most home and small-office setups.
Worth flagging before you buy: this is a brand-new launch, so there are no independent reviews yet to verify GMKtec's performance and AI TOPS figures - although the previous model impressed us throughout our testing (you can read the review here).
And while the Radeon 890M handles mainstream gaming reasonably well, you'll need to add an external GPU over OCuLink for serious 1440p or 4K gaming performance.
For anyone wanting a compact desktop that can run local AI workloads today and take a discrete GPU down the line, the Evo-X1 Pro is a genuinely interesting new option.

articles.title: Microsoft's stock rises 9% on strong Azure revenue growth and steady capex spending - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Microsoft’s stock rises 9% on strong Azure revenue growth and steady capex spending
Microsoft Corp.’s stock was trading 9% higher in the after-hours session today after reporting four-quarter earnings and revenue that surpassed Wall Street’s expectations while reiterating its capital expenditures forecast for the rest of the year.
The company reported earnings before certain costs such as stock compensation of $4.74 per share, beating the Street’s projection of $4.24 per share, but there was a caveat to those results. The figure includes 27 cents of unusual accounting benefits mostly derived from a $3.2 billion unrealized gain on Microsoft’s investment in Anthropic PBC. During the quarter, Anthropic’s valuation jumped from $350 billion to $900 billion.
The company also reported revenue of $90.01 billion, up 18% from a year earlier and above the Street’s target of $87.62 billion. All told, it delivered net income of $35.77 billion in the quarter, up from $27.23 billion in the year-ago period.
Microsoft’s stock is still down 19% in the year to date, trailing the broader S&P 500 index, which has gained around 7% so far this year. Investors have put software stocks under pressure this year amid fears of disruption caused by artificial intelligence agents. At the same time, Microsoft also faces some “concentration risk” stemming from its close relationship with OpenAI Group PBC and the rise of open-source AI models, said analysts from Deutsche Bank in a note earlier this week. Last January, Microsoft revealed that around $45 billion of its $625 billion in commercial remaining performance obligations were tied to OpenAI’s future success.
On a conference call with analysts, Microsoft Chief Executive Satya Nadella (pictured) said the company has been trying to balance the needs of Azure cloud customers, AI research and applications such as the Microsoft 365 Copilot assistant. If it devotes more chips to its research teams for model training, that means having less available for cloud customers to use, he explained.
Microsoft’s finance chief Amy Hood said the company’s commercial RPO, which is a measure of booked but unearned revenue, rose 8% to $678 billion at the end of the quarter on a sequential basis, due to commitments from clients other than AI model developers. The company spent $41 billion on capital expenditures and leases during the quarter, up 69% from a year ago.
Hood reiterated the company’s capex spending plans over the rest of the calendar year, and it’s likely that investors were relieved to see no increases, unlike at some of its cloud rivals. She said the company also plans to lengthen the useful life of its new offices and data center buildings to 25 years, instead of 15 years as before. Moreover, the company plans to switch more of its leases from finance leases to operating leases in future, with the adjustments expected to lead to roughly $175 billion in capex.
In the days preceding the report, there was a lot of concern that Microsoft’s capital outlays might be outpacing the momentum behind Azure and Copilot AI, but today’s results appear to have quelled those fears, said Valoir analyst Rebecca Wettemann. But Microsoft still has work to do if it’s to convince all of the naysayers, especially where OpenAI is concerned, she said.
“We still need to see real ROI around both vendors’ AI and data center investments and customers’ token spend,” Wettemann explained. “Those that were burned with unsuccessful expensive experiments early on are hesitant to move AI to production now unless they’re sure it will perform as promised and not ring up a big unexpected token bill overnight, and Microsoft and others need to do others to help calm enterprise AI ‘fear of messing up’ and ensure they’re helping customers deploy AI at scale that delivers ROI and minimizes risk.”
For fiscal 2027, Hood said the company is planning to increase its capex spending in order to pursue “demand signals across our portfolio.” Looking to the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Hood said Microsoft is targeting revenue of between $89.85 billion to $90.95 billion, ahead of the $89.71 billion analyst forecast.
“Capex is still something to watch carefully,” Wettemann said. “Whatever Microsoft communicates over the next few quarters will be really important, in terms of what it’s building from an infrastructure perspective but also what investments it’s making to make Azure cloud and its AI deliver more efficiently and cost-effectively for customers.
Breaking down the numbers from today’s results, Microsoft’s Intelligent Cloud segment, which includes revenue from the Azure cloud, posted $39.31 billion in sales, up 32% from the previous year and above the Street’s $38.16 billion consensus estimate. Azure growth accelerated to 43%, up from 40% in the previous quarter and above the 40% analyst forecast.
Hood said the company expects Azure revenue to grow at 45% in the current quarter, ahead of the Street’s consensus of 41.4%.
Emarketer analyst Gadjo Sevilla told SiliconANGLE that Microsoft’s solid numbers appear to have caused investors to have a bit of a rethink about its stock valuation. “Azure was central to the story, with Nadella saying that Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the full year for the first time,” he said. “CFO Amy Hood highlighted Microsoft Cloud revenue of $59.3 billion for the quarter, up 27% YoY, likely on the strength of AI dependencies.”
Elsewhere, Microsoft’s Productivity and Business segment, which includes sales from Office, Dynamics and LinkedIn, recorded revenue of $37.85 billion in the quarter, up 14% and ahead of the $37.19 billion analyst target. Nadella said on the call that the company now has more than 30 million paid seats for Microsoft 365 Copilot, with hundreds of enterprise customers purchasing seats for high-end E7 productivity software bundles. He added that the GitHub Copilot coding assistant now exceeds more than 50 million users.
The More Personal Computing segment, which includes Windows, Bing, Surface and Xbox console sales, generated $12.85 billion in revenue, down 4% from a year earlier but above the Street’s $12.17 billion target. Sales of devices and Windows licenses to device makers dropped 7% compared to the same quarter last year, in line with a report by the research firm Gartner Inc. that personal computer sales declined 4.2% during the quarter. Xbox revenue dropped 10%, and earlier this month, the company said it would be forced to increase the cost of new consoles due to the rising price of memory chips, which are a key component of them.

articles.title: Celular Xiaomi com NFC: 7 smartphones para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Celular Xiaomi com NFC: 7 smartphones para comprar em 2026
Encontre o melhor Xiaomi com NFC para pagamentos por aproximação e saiba como identificar se um smartphone tem a tecnologia
Encontre o melhor Xiaomi com NFC para pagamentos por aproximação e saiba como identificar se um smartphone tem a tecnologia
Escolher um celular Xiaomi com NFC é a decisão ideal para quem busca praticidade ao realizar pagamentos por aproximação no dia a dia. A tecnologia aproxima o smartphone do terminal de pagamento e garante transações financeiras rápidas e seguras.
O catálogo da fabricante chinesa oferece modelos versáteis com conectividade NFC nativa, suporte a redes 5G, telas AMOLED de alta qualidade e excelente autonomia de bateria.
Confira nossa seleção com os melhores celulares das linhas Xiaomi, Poco e Redmi para comprar em 2026.
⚠️ Verifique a ficha técnica
A Xiaomi comercializa diferentes versões de um mesmo produto globalmente, e a conectividade NFC é dependente do mercado/região. Antes de finalizar a compra, verifique a ficha técnica e/ou pergunte ao vendedor se o smartphone pretendido conta com a tecnologia.
O Xiaomi 17T é um smartphone premium da marca à venda no Brasil, e conta com recursos de conectividade avançados, incluindo NFC. O celular tem processador MediaTek Dimensity 8500-Ultra, armazenamento de 512 GB e 12 GB de RAM para alto desempenho.
Nos testes do Tecnoblog, a bateria de 6.500 mAh entregou boa autonomia mesmo sob uso intenso, e as câmeras entregaram ótimos resultados em fotos de perto ou de longe.
O Poco F8 Pro é um celular topo de linha focado em desempenho, com o processador Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite em litografia de 3 nm, 12 GB de RAM e armazenamento interno de 256 GB ou 512 GB. Além do NFC, o smartphone conta com 5G, Bluetooth 5.4 e Wi-Fi 7.
A tela AMOLED de 6,59 polegadas oferece taxa de atualização de 120 Hz, com suporte a Dolby Vision e HDR10+. E bateria de 6.210 mAh tem carregamento rápido com fio de até 100 W.
O Poco X8 Pro também traz conectividade avançada com NFC, 5G e Bluetooth 6.0, além de Wi-Fi 6.
O celular equilibra alto poder de fogo e boa autonomia de bateria na categoria intermediária com o chip MediaTek Dimensity 8500-Ultra, opções de 8 GB ou 12 GB de RAM e 256 GB ou 512 GB de armazenamento.
A bateria de 6.500 mAh tem recarga rápida de 100 W. Em nossos testes, o componente durou cerca de três dias em uso diário e cerca de 20 horas em reprodução contínua com brilho máximo e tela em 120 Hz.
O Redmi Note 15 Pro é um celular intermediário com NFC. O dispositivo foca em durabilidade, tela ampla e câmeras. O modelo conta com painel AMOLED de 6,83 polegadas com proteção Corning Gorilla Glass Victus 2 e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz.
A construção possui certificação IP68 contra água e poeira, que foi testada pelo Tecnoblog em uma trilha de três horas sob sol e chuva e uma sessão de mergulho de 40 minutos.
O modelo usa o processador MediaTek Dimensity 7400-Ultra, com opções de 8 GB ou 12 GB de RAM e armazenamento interno de 256 GB ou 512 GB. No sistema de câmeras, há um sensor principal de 200 MP com OIS, gravando em até 4K, além de ultrawide de 8 MP e frontal de 20 MP.
O Xiaomi 15T é um smartphone avançado lançado em 2025 com NFC, Bluetooth 6.0, Wi-Fi 6e e 5G.
Um destaque é a tela AMOLED de 6,83 polegadas, com resolução 1.5K, taxa de atualização de 120 Hz e pico de brilho de até 3.200 nits. As câmeras também são um ponto positivo, com lentes com tecnologia Leica Summilux e sensor principal de 50 MP (com OIS).
O desempenho fica a cargo do processador MediaTek Dimensity 8400-Ultra com 12 GB de RAM e 256 GB ou 512 GB de armazenamento UFS 4.1. A bateria é de 5.500 mAh com carregamento HyperCharge de 67 W.
O Poco X7 Pro é um celular intermediário conhecido pelo bom custo-benefício. Além de NFC, ele conta com 5G, Bluetooth 5.4 e Wi-Fi 6.
O alto desempenho é garantido pelo chip MediaTek Dimensity 8400-Ultra, memória RAM LPDDR5X de 8 GB ou 12 GB e armazenamento UFS 4.0 de 256 GB ou 512 GB.
O painel é um AMOLED de 6,67 polegadas com resolução 1.5K, taxa de 120 Hz e suporte a Dolby Vision e HDR10+. A bateria possui capacidade de 6.000 mAh com recarga rápida de 90 W.
O Redmi 15C 5G é um smartphone básico com NFC. O celular tem preço na faixa dos R$ 1 mil e entrega desempenho satisfatório para navegação em redes sociais, consumo de vídeos e navegação. No entanto, o desempenho é limitado em multitarefa e jogos exigentes.
A tela de 120 Hz entrega boa fluidez gráfica, mas a tecnologia LCD do painel resulta em contrastes menos intensos e um preto acinzentado.
O celular entrega boa autonomia de bateria com 6.000 mAh e carregamento rápido de 33 W.
Considere esses três fatores principais antes de comprar um celular Xiaomi com NFC:

Por isso, é importante verificar com o vendedor se a tecnologia está habilitada no modelo que você pretende comprar.
Não. O NFC é um componente de hardware que precisa vir instalado de fábrica na placa-mãe do celular.
Faça o seguinte para descobrir se o celular tem NFC:
Alguns celulares Xiaomi não têm NFC pelos seguintes motivos:
Sim, é seguro pagar com NFC. Os celulares Xiaomi utilizam a Google Wallet para fazer pagamentos por aproximação. Assim, os aparelhos passam a utilizar os mesmos mecanismos de segurança dos celulares de outras marcas, como Motorola e Samsung.

articles.title: Relic Entertainment Company of Heroes 3: Final Stand Out Now
articles.text:
Wednesday, July 29th 2026
	
	
	
	Relic Entertainment Company of Heroes 3: Final Stand Out Now
Relic Entertainment today announced that Company of Heroes 3: Final Stand is now available on Steam for $29.99 USD / £23.99 GBP / €28.99 EUR with a 10% introductory discount for two weeks, alongside an additional 20% bundle discount for existing Company of Heroes 3 owners. Available as a standalone product, Final Stand captures the strategy and intensity of Company of Heroes' cinematic battles in a fast-paced wave defense experience for solo and cooperative play.
Built on the beloved tactical foundation of Company of Heroes, Final Stand expands the series' signature combat with roguelite progression that encourages experimentation, adaptation, and replayability. Players must dig in, build layered defenses, and survive against escalating waves of enemy forces across 12 increasingly challenging rounds, featuring intimidating bosses and dynamic battlefield events unique to Final Stand.Launching during the franchise's 20th anniversary celebration, Final Stand introduces an intense wave defense experience inspired by Relic's legacy of fan-favorite survival modes, blending cinematic battlefield action with roguelite progression systems that create a new strategic experience with every run.
Built for both single-player and cooperative play, Final Stand challenges players to hold the line through 12 escalating waves of increasingly dangerous enemy forces. Between rounds, players construct custom battlegroups by selecting randomized units and abilities that persist throughout each run, ensuring no two battles unfold the same way.
Players can command one of four iconic factions:
Beyond individual runs, players unlock persistent progression through faction-specific upgrade trees, earning powerful perks and abilities that encourage experimentation, mastery, and higher-level challenges.

Between rounds, players construct custom battlegroups by selecting randomized units and abilities that persist throughout each run, ensuring no two battles unfold the same way.
Players can command one of four iconic factions:
- US Forces
- Wehrmacht
- British Forces
- Deutsches Afrikakorps
Beyond individual runs, players unlock persistent progression through faction-specific upgrade trees, earning powerful perks and abilities that encourage experimentation, mastery, and higher-level challenges.
Key Features
- All-new standalone Company of Heroes wave defense experience
- Single-player and 2-player cooperative gameplay
- Command 4 iconic factions with unique strategies and progression paths
- Roguelite progression that creates new strategic possibilities every run
- 36 boss units featuring unique abilities and rewards
- 18 dynamic battlefield events
- 8 difficulty levels ranging from newcomer to veteran
- 5 battlegrounds purpose-built for wave defense gameplay
- Survive 12 escalating waves or test your limits in Endless Mode
- Faction-specific progression trees with impactful upgrades
- Unlock 4 premium cosmetic skin packs
- Brand-new announcer voice performances

Points forts Écran bien calibré et très lumineux. Présence du Snapdragon 8 Elite. Volet photo complet. Excellente autonomie. Expérience One UI 7. Points faibles Design déjà vu. Téléobjectif assez décevant. Charge limitée à 25 W en 2025 !? Alors oui, ce Galaxy S25 a tout d’un S24 amélioré, mais le résultat est là : le millésime 2025 surpasse le précédent. Son format compact, son écran réussi et sa puce surpuissante et économe en énergie en font un modèle aussi fluide qu’endurant. L’expérience photo gagne en précision, même si tout n’est pas parfait, notamment du côté du téléobjectif. On peut aussi regretter une puissance de charge encore limitée par rapport à la concurrence. Cependant, l’expérience offerte par One UI 7 et les nombreuses fonctions d’IA apportent un vent de modernité. À moins de posséder le modèle de 2024, cette itération est donc hautement recommandable. Samsung prouve ici que dans la tech comme en amour, il ne faut pas se fier aux apparences, et que l’important, c’est ce qu’il y a à l’intérieur.

articles.title: Reclámalo antes del 30 de julio: aclamado juego de cartas y decisiones que Epic Games está regalando
articles.text:
Epic Games Store vuelve a captar la atención de jugadores de todo el mundo con una nueva promoción semanal: un aclamado juego de cartas y toma de decisiones puede reclamarse gratis hasta el 30 de julio y quedarse para siempre en tu biblioteca digital.
Se trata de una oportunidad limitada para sumar una experiencia narrativa diferente, sin coste y sin condiciones ocultas. Tras esa fecha, la tienda renovará su oferta y añadirá nuevos títulos gratuitos, por lo que conviene no dejar pasar la oportunidad.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuál es el juego gratuito de la semana en Epic Games
El protagonista de la semana es Foretales, una aventura que mezcla construcción de mazos, exploración y decisiones ramificadas. No es un simple juego de cartas: combina elementos de rol, puzles y narrativa, permitiendo que cada partida sea única y que las elecciones influyan directamente en el desenlace.
La mecánica de reclamar y conservarlo gratis se mantiene: una vez añadido a la cuenta, el título puede instalarse y jugarse en cualquier momento, sin restricciones ni necesidad de suscripción.
PUBLICIDAD
Foretales destaca por su propuesta narrativa y estratégica. El jugador asume el papel de un héroe que debe navegar un mundo de fantasía enfrentando desafíos donde el ingenio y la gestión del mazo son tan importantes como la toma de decisiones morales. Cada encuentro puede resolverse de diversas formas, desde el combate hasta la diplomacia, lo que multiplica las posibilidades de juego y fomenta la rejugabilidad.
El arte visual y la ambientación suman a la experiencia, ofreciendo una estética de libro ilustrado y una banda sonora envolvente. La combinación de puzles, narrativa y estrategia convierte a Foretales en una opción atractiva para quienes buscan algo más que acción directa, apostando por la profundidad y la creatividad.
PUBLICIDAD
La promoción está disponible hasta el 30 de julio a las 17:00 (hora peninsular española), o a las 10:00 en Ciudad de México. Una vez finalizado ese plazo, el título dejará de estar gratis y será reemplazado por otras ofertas semanales.
Cómo reclamar Foretales gratis en Epic Games Store
El proceso es rápido y accesible para cualquier usuario, incluso sin experiencia previa en la plataforma:
- Crear o iniciar sesión en tu cuenta Epic Games Accede a (store.epicgames.com), regístrate con tu correo electrónico o inicia sesión si ya eres usuario.
- Ir a la sección Tienda Desde la página principal, ingresa a la pestaña “Tienda” para ver los títulos destacados y los juegos gratuitos de la semana.
- Ubicar el juego gratuito Foretales Busca Foretales entre los juegos promocionados como gratuitos y haz clic en su ficha.
- Procesar la compra a coste cero Verifica que el precio sea “0” y pulsa en “Obtener”. Completa la transacción sin ingresar datos de pago.
- Agregar el juego a tu biblioteca Una vez terminado el proceso, el título quedará vinculado a tu cuenta de forma permanente, permitiendo futuras descargas sin restricciones.
- Instalar y jugar Descarga el cliente de Epic Games Store, accede a tu biblioteca, elige el juego y comienza la instalación en tu ordenador. Revisa los requisitos técnicos para asegurar el mejor rendimiento.
Ventajas y recomendaciones del formato digital
El auge de la distribución digital ha transformado la industria del videojuego. Plataformas como Epic Games Store y Steam permiten disfrutar de lanzamientos inmediatos, actualizaciones frecuentes y una variedad de títulos sin precedentes. Reclamar juegos gratis es una forma inteligente de ampliar tu colección, descubrir géneros nuevos y apoyar a desarrolladores independientes.
PUBLICIDAD
Estos títulos permanecen en tu biblioteca aunque los desinstales, y pueden reinstalarse en cualquier momento siempre que conserves el acceso a tu cuenta. Es recomendable revisar la tienda semanalmente y activar notificaciones para no perder futuras promociones. Si bien el formato digital no permite la reventa, sí brinda comodidad, acceso global y la posibilidad de disfrutar de nuevas aventuras sin coste alguno.
Foretales es solo el primero de más lanzamientos gratuitos que llegarán próximamente a Epic Games Store, consolidando a la plataforma como un referente en la distribución de videojuegos digitales y en el apoyo a propuestas innovadoras.

articles.title: IoT Tech Expo Europe Returns to Amsterdam as Industrial AI and Edge Intelligence Reshape Connected Industry - EE Times
articles.text:
https://www.iottechexpo.com/europe/
From autonomous factories and AI-powered robots to connected vehicles and smart cities, organizations are entering a new era where connected systems are expected not only to collect data, but also to analyze, decide, and act in real time.
As Industrial IoT continues to evolve, the focus has shifted beyond deploying connected devices. Today’s challenge is combining Artificial Intelligence, Edge AI, advanced connectivity, and secure embedded systems to create intelligent, resilient operations that deliver measurable business value at scale.
These developments will take center stage at IoT Tech Expo Europe, returning to the RAI Amsterdam on 19-20 October 2026 as part of TechEx Europe.
The event comes at a pivotal moment for the IoT industry. Manufacturers are accelerating Industrial AI initiatives, cities are investing in smarter infrastructure, organisations are deploying Edge AI to reduce latency and improve decision-making, and new cybersecurity regulations are placing greater emphasis on protecting connected devices throughout their lifecycle. As these technologies converge, businesses face growing pressure to move beyond pilot projects and successfully deploy Industrial IoT solutions at scale.
“The IoT landscape is evolving incredibly quickly, so we’ve built this year’s agenda around the technologies and deployment challenges organizations are dealing with right now,” said Michael Hughes, Head of Conference at TechEx Events. “Whether it’s scaling Industrial AI, deploying Edge AI, securing connected devices or building the infrastructure for smarter cities, every session is designed to provide practical insight from the organizations leading these transformations. Our focus is on helping attendees understand not just what’s next, but what’s working today.”
Reflecting these priorities, the conference programme at IoT Tech Expo Europe is built around four key themes shaping the future of connected industry: Industrial AI and Autonomous Operations, Connectivity, Infrastructure and Smart Cities, Edge AI and Real-Time Intelligence, and IoT Security and Embedded Systems.
The agenda is supported by experts from organisations including Schneider Electric, Bosch, Electrolux Group, Volvo Group, BMW Group, Capgemini, NXP Semiconductors, Infineon Technologies, Emerson, Renault Group, and DHL Supply Chain, alongside many other organisations driving innovation across manufacturing, automotive, logistics, and critical infrastructure.
Industrial AI, Connectivity, and Smart Infrastructure
Day one of IoT Tech Expo Europe explores how organisations are applying Industrial AI across manufacturing, logistics, and critical infrastructure. Sessions will examine autonomous operations, robotics, digital twins, and predictive maintenance, alongside the connectivity technologies supporting these intelligent environments.
The program also explores private 5G, satellite IoT, resilient network infrastructure, and the role of connected technologies in building smarter cities and modernizing public infrastructure, highlighting how connectivity is becoming the foundation for intelligent, autonomous operations.
Edge AI, IoT Security, and Embedded Systems
On the second day, IoT Tech Expo Europe turns its attention to the technologies enabling real-time intelligence at the edge.
Sessions will explore how organisations are deploying Edge AI, computer vision, and embedded systems closer to where data is generated, reducing latency while improving operational performance and resilience. As connected devices continue to increase across industrial and enterprise environments, cybersecurity remains a central focus, with discussions covering IoT Security, embedded engineering, device resilience, compliance, and strategies for protecting connected infrastructure throughout its lifecycle.
The programme will also examine how organisations are embedding intelligence directly into devices, enabling faster decision-making while reducing dependence on centralised cloud infrastructure and unlocking new opportunities across Industrial IoT deployments.
With more than 200 speakers participating across the wider TechEx Europe programme, IoT Tech Expo Europe offers practical insight from organisations deploying AI-powered IoT solutions across factories, supply chains, connected vehicles, smart infrastructure, and industrial operations.
For IoT leaders, enterprise architects, engineers, and technology decision-makers, IoT Tech Expo Europe provides an opportunity to explore how Industrial AI, Edge AI, secure connectivity, and embedded intelligence are reshaping Industrial IoT, while learning directly from the organizations delivering these technologies in the real world.
IoT Tech Expo Europe takes place on 19-20 October 2026 at the RAI Amsterdam as part of TechEx Europe. Registration is now open, with complimentary expo passes and paid conference passes available via the TechEx Europe website.

articles.title: OpenAI opens new ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to 100,000 scientists - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
OpenAI opens new ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to 100,000 scientists
OpenAI Group PBC today launched a program that will give 100,000 researchers free access to ChatGPT’s advanced features.
ChatGPT for Academic Researchers is part of a $250 million OpenAI initiative designed to support scientific projects. The initiative also includes several other programs. Last May, OpenAI made $50 million worth of artificial intelligence resources available to a group of universities. This month, it announced plans to support multiple U.S. Energy Department research projects.
Scientists can apply to ChatGPT for Academic Researchers via a form on OpenAI’s website. Initially, the program will be open to 10,000 users at a limited number of universities. OpenAI plans to onboard 90,000 more researchers over time.
According to the company, participants will receive access to a version of ChatGPT with “higher usage limits and larger context windows.” OpenAI also plans to provide an “expanded” edition of the chatbot service’s deep research feature. The capability, which debuted last February, can collect information from hundreds of websites to answer user questions. Researchers can alternatively configure it to focus on specific sources such as scientific journals.
A scientist who is invited to OpenAI’s new program can onboard four colleagues from the same academic institution. Those researchers receive access to the same set of features at no charge.
According to OpenAI, the version of ChatGPT offered through the program ships with its latest large language models. The includes the company’s flagship GPT-5.6 Sol algorithm. In particular, scientists will receive access to a version of the LLM called GPT-5.6 Sol Pro that is optimized for difficult queries and long-running tasks.
The program also includes Codex and ChatGPT Work. The latter tool, the latest addition to OpenAI’s lineup of productivity features, can automate sequences of relatively complex tasks. For example, a user could ask ChatGPT Work to summarize a set of customer support requests, turn the key findings into a graph and then embed the graph in a slide.
The program also includes certain supporting resources. OpenAI will provide training on how to apply ChatGPT to complex research tasks. Additionally, the company’s employees will help scientists integrate the service with their other scientific applications.
OpenAI first moved into the higher education sector in 2024 by launching a ChatGPT plan called Edu. It includes cybersecurity controls, a usage analytics dashboard and other administrative features.
ChatGPT for Academic Researchers could prove conducive to OpenAI’s revenue growth efforts in the sector. If a small number of researchers at an academic department sign up to the program and start using ChatGPT, some of their colleagues may follow suit. Those users, in turn, might purchase ChatGPT subscriptions or develop software that connects to OpenAI’s paid application programming interface.

articles.title: Drones contra campers: Ibiza ha entrado en una caza constante contra los trabajadores que no se pueden pagar una casa
articles.text:
España vive sus pequeñas batallas aéreas y en todas ellas los drones son protagonistas. No hablamos de ataques contra infraestructuras clave. Hablamos de la administración utilizando el cielo para detectar infracciones. Para ver si te saltas un Stop o para ver si has construido una piscina. También para certificar que no estás viviendo donde toca. Por turismo o, sencillamente, porque no puedes permitirte otra cosa.
Eso está pasando en Ibiza.
200 personas. Es, más o menos, el número de personas que han sido desalojadas de los asentamientos de Sa Joveria y Can Misses en Ibiza, explican nuestros compañeros de Motorpasión. El motivo es tan sencillo como que viven en un caravana.
Como señalan en este medio, no hablamos de turistas, hablamos de trabajadores que no pueden permitirse vivir en una casa porque el precio de las habitaciones y de las viviendas es tan desorbitado que a las personas empleadas en la isla viven en una paradoja: necesitan el trabajo para vivir pero ese mismo trabajo no les da para vivir.
Los drones. Para vigilar asentamientos como estos, las administraciones están empleando drones que desde el aire vigilan si una caravana está aparcada entre los árboles de una zona frondosa, fuera de un camping. La campaña, incluso, ha empezado meses atrás. En abril ya se registraron los desalojos de los dos centenares de personas mencionadas más arriba.
El ayuntamiento de Sant Josep se ha convertido en el primero de Europa en tener un dron autónomo mejorado con IA para su policía. Los drones, aseguran, ayudarán en casos de accidentes de coches o labores de búsqueda de personas pero también controlan labores de "vigilancia medioambiental, detección de vertidos ilegales, disciplina urbanística y protección de espacios naturales", explican en Periódico de Ibiza. Algo parecido sucede en Sant Antoni de Portmany.
Una pinza. Estas últimas labores son las esgrimidas por las autoridades para desmontar lo que consideran asentamientos ilegales. Para evitar que el turismo de caravanas no colapsara la isla, en 2024 idearon una nueva normativa que limita el número de vehículos que pueden entrar a la isla. En el caso de las caravanas no pueden entrar si no tienen una plaza de parking ya reservada.
Para desalojar de forma express a estos vehículos, la Ley del Suelo Rústico de las Baleares se ha convertido en el mejor arma. Y es que desde que se activó esta normativa, suelo rústico es prácticamente cualquier espacio que no se encuentra en una zona urbana. Acampar aquí puede llegar a conllevar una multa de hasta 30.000 euros por lo que los afectados abandonan rápidamente estos espacios cuando son informados de la posible sanción a la que se enfrentan.
El verdadero problema es que estas personas de las que hablamos no son turistas, son trabajadores que no tienen un techo (al menos sin ruedas) donde puedan vivir. El exceso de turismo ha provocado que las administraciones impulsen normativas cada vez más rígidas y ahora esos trabajadores se encuentran en mitad de una dolorosa pinza, turistas a un lado, reguladores a otro y drones por encima de sus cabezas.
¿Es tanto el problema? Ya en mayo señalábamos que para poder alquilar un piso de 80 metros cuadrados en Ibiza necesitabas cobrar 2.320 euros mensuales. Eso suponiendo que no gastaras ni un solo euro en comer, en encender las luces de casa o en darte una ducha.
Y es que el precio de las viviendas es tan disparatado que hay vecinos que, por sí mismos, deciden irse a vivir a una caravana durante los meses de temporada alta. La idea es tan simple como la de dejar la casa a turistas adinerados para sacarse un sobresueldo. Con una presión turística insoportable y sin viviendas suficientes, un buen número de profesionales buscan acomodo en una suerte de casa con ruedas.
"Empezamos a buscar casa, pero fue una locura ver lo que pedían […] Entonces comenzamos a mirar lo que costaba una caravana de segunda mano y fue la única opción que vimos para quedarnos", recogían en Periódico de Ibiza. Las palabras son de Mariana Gómez, una mujer que viajó a Ibiza desde Colombia para trabajar de forma temporal en un hotel y que acabó llegando a la conclusión de que, si quería instalarse en la isla junto a su pareja, no le quedaba otra que renunciar a los pisos "normales"… y optar por una caravana.
Y algunos motivos hay. Aunque desolador, los ayuntamientos y los reguladores tienen sus propios motivos para desalojar estos campamentos. En Sa Joveria aseguran que se habían retirado 5.000 kg de basura durante uno de los desalojos. Sus responsables aseguraban a Cadena Ser que éste no se había llevado a cabo tanto por detectar viviendas ilegales si no por "las quejas por las malas condiciones".
Este mismo mes de julio, Noudiari.es explicaba en un artículo que en Cala Bou se había detectado un nuevo asentamiento ilegal del que salían "personas aparentemente trabajadoras que salían con sus mochilas camino de sus puestos de trabajo". El problema, señalaban, es que "no se aprecia desde fuera una gran acumulación de basuras pero sí que hay restos por el perímetro y en algunos puntos se puede apreciar claramente el olor a orina y excrementos".
Por lo tanto, el riesgo para el deterioro del medio ambiente y el riesgo de incendio aumentan exponencialmente en estos casos.

articles.title: GlobalFoundries Receives $300M for Silicon Photonics, U.S. Government Acquires 1% Stake
articles.text:
Wednesday, July 29th 2026
	
		
	
	
	GlobalFoundries Receives $300M for Silicon Photonics, U.S. Government Acquires 1% Stake
GlobalFoundries announced today that the United States Government, under the administration of Donald J. Trump, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce to advance next-generation silicon photonics technologies. Notably, GlobalFoundries will receive $300 million from the CHIPS Act fund, while the U.S. Government will acquire approximately a 1% equity stake in the company. As some may recall, GlobalFoundries ceased its efforts in leading-edge node research, development, and manufacturing just as the industry was transitioning to 7 nm. However, the company has since shifted its focus to other technologies, such as silicon photonics, which are becoming increasingly valuable in the era of AI expansion.
GlobalFoundries stated that this funding will be used to develop next-generation silicon photonics and advanced packaging, focusing on near-packaged optics (NPO), co-packaged optics (CPO), 3D hybrid bonding, and novel material development. The company recently introduced its SCALE (Silicon Photonics Co-Packaged Advanced Light Engine) platform, which supports 400 Gb/s package transfers with high energy efficiency. They plan to invest these R&D funds in their manufacturing facilities in Malta, New York, and Burlington, Vermont, fulfilling their commitment to develop manufacturing capabilities on U.S. soil.Several SCALE CPO and NPO customers provided statements for this announcement, including AMD, Broadcom, Cisco, Corning, Lumentum, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Qualcomm. Many of these companies praised silicon photonics for helping with fast data movement by using light instead of copper, overcoming previous technological challenges as copper hits its limits. They also expressed satisfaction with the onshoring of U.S.-based technology, which strengthens the supply chain.

articles.title: Pennsylvania town lists 43 specific demands to approve new AI data center project — developer calls local demands 'too difficult' as council slams response as 'approval by tantrum'
articles.text:
Pennsylvania town lists 43 specific demands to approve new AI data center project — developer calls local demands 'too difficult' as council slams response as 'approval by tantrum'
The township says this is ‘a blatant attempt by the Applicant to demand approval by tantrum.’
Plymouth Township, which sits roughly 13 miles to the north of Philadelphia, said that it will approve a new data center project on the condition that it meets 43 specific demands. While Pennsylvania state law prohibits blocking a landowner from using their property lawfully, Ars Technica says that townships can impose zoning restrictions and health and safety regulations. Because of this, Plymouth created a nine-page plan that covers everything from noise, light, and air pollution, to water and power use, as well as land use, taxes, and even future decommissioning of the data center.
Many jurisdictions would have just outright rejected or delayed the data center project, which is owned by Brian O’Neill, but Plymouth Township decided to go in a different direction. It still allowed the application to go through, as not doing so would expose the local government to legal action, but gave the developer the outlined demands (listed in pages 4 to 12 of this PDF) that it needs to meet to get the green light from its people. The township said that the applicant initially showed that they would implement that township’s provisions, which were derived from the demands of its residents.
“The Council can, should, and will do everything in its power to ensure the health, safety, and welfare of the Township, our environment, and our residents. This is always our top priority,” Council President Lynne Viscio said in a statement. “We understand that a hyperscale data center raises numerous significant concerns, issues, and questions. Accordingly, we spent considerable time researching and developing a comprehensive set of requirements to address the concerns raised by residents, our own concerns, and the issues raised by other subject matter experts.”
Unfortunately, the data center developer rejected the concerns after seeing the breakdown of demands. It then filed a second application challenging the provisions set in the zoning ordinance, saying that they make building the project “too difficult” for the developer. Plymouth Township did not look kindly upon this, saying it “is a blatant attempt by the Applicant to demand approval by tantrum.” It’s currently unclear how Plymouth Township will move forward with the issue, with the application currently awaiting approval from the Zoning Hearing Board.
As for O’Neill, he told the Philadelphia Inquirer that the accusations of was part of a “misinformation campaign” against his project, and that he has been “negotiating in good faith” with the township’s attorney and had even agreed to most of the provisions. “We are sympathetic to the fact that they are under tremendous political scrutiny from people outside the township, as well as residents inside the township, and that makes giving a landowner their property rights … challenging,” he told the local newspaper. “However, I am a landowner, and I do have rights, and it is their job to be impartial and fair in their analysis and response.”
These requirements are meant to prevent the various challenges that other communities face with data center deployments. Examples of these include a Michigan data center generating noise 24/7 that has been affecting residents for over two years, PJM Interconnection, the U.S.’s largest power region, hiking electricity prices by 76% due to AI demand, a Meta data center contaminating a city’s reclamation water supply, and Elon Musk’s Colossus 2 data center facing a lawsuit for its unpermitted natural gas turbines spewing nitrogen oxides and other pollutants.
